parole.significato: Any of ten former territories defined as homelands for black South Africans under apartheid policy
parole.testo: From a Bantu language (ultimately from Proto-Bantu *bantʊ̀ (“people”)) + -stan (“home of”, suffix of Persian origin), after place names such as Hindustan.

parole.significato: The African tropical hardwood of the tree Nauclea diderrichii.
parole.testo: Borrowed from certain Gabonese Bantu (cf. Myene mbilinga, Barama mbilinga, Sangu (Gabon) mbilinga, Lumbu mbilinga, Ngubi mbilinga, Sira mbilinga, Vumbu mbilinga, Viya mbilinga, Benga mbilinga).

parole.significato: Pan troglodytes, a species of great ape native to the savannas and forests of Africa, and believed by biologists to be…
parole.testo: The first recorded use of the name chimpanzee dates to 1738. The name is derived from an unspecified Bantu language of Angola (compare Vili ci-mpenzi), probably brought to the English language via French chimpanzé.

parole.significato: A bushbuck (Tragelaphus sylvaticus), one of two species, ranging more into southern and eastern Africa than the other s…

parole.motivo_incerta: Of uncertain origin; Probably; perhaps; alternatively
parole.testo: Probably a clipping of jigaboo, of uncertain origin, perhaps an African/Bantu word. Alternatively, jigaboo may be derived from jig (“dance”).
Possibly an African word akin to Bantu tshikabo (“they bow the head docilely”). Alternatively, perhaps from jig, formed similarly to bug and bugaboo.

parole.significato: A former unit of currency, one hundredth of a zaïre.
parole.testo: From a Bantu language spoken in the Congo region. Compare Lingala li- + -kútá. Perhaps ultimately from Kongo nkúta (“provisions”).

parole.significato: A tree of species Baillonella toxisperma, found throughout subtropical forests of Africa, used for its oil.
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Gabonese or Congolese Bantu language: compare Sira moabi, Barama moabi, Vumbu moabi, Punu moabi, Lumbu moabi, Sangu (Gabon) moabi, Ngubi moabi, Duma muyabi, Ibhili muyavi, Njebi muyèbi, moyabi, muyabi, Vili moabi, Yombe moabi, Yaa moyabi, muyabi, Teke-Laali moyabi, muyabi).

parole.significato: Transvaal teak, the timber tree Pterocarpus angolensis, or its substitute of comparable properties Pterocarpus tinctori…
parole.testo: Borrowed from various Bantu languages, where the mu- or m- represents the noun class prefix.

parole.significato: A style of music and a rhythm associated with the sect and ceremony, and with reggae music.
parole.testo: Most likely from a Great Lakes Bantu language. Compare Tooro -nya- (“pertaining to”) and ingi (“rich in; plentiful in”). The spelling with -gh- may reflect an early spelling of /ŋɡ/ to distinguish it from the simple /ŋ/.
Borrowed from certain Gabonese Bantu (Cf. Myene okumé, Viya okumé, Tsogo okumé) via French okoumé.

parole.significato: Any of the prominent cultural ruins of which Greater Zimbabwe is the most well known.
parole.testo: From the Bantu word for a meeting house.
